thread.title: Not Smart To Short Eric Sprott's Kirkland Lake And Novo Resources - Kirkland Lake Gold Ltd. (NYSE:KL)

author: Jeb Handwerger
title: Not Smart To Short Eric Sprott's Kirkland Lake And Novo Resources - Kirkland Lake Gold Ltd. (NYSE:KL)

organizations.name: novo resources - kirkland lake gold ltd.

text:
Junior gold exploration ( GDX ) is a crazy business with valuations that can be all over the map. You can find a gold miner permitted in production trading at fractions of a new gold explorer with a theory. This may be what has taken place in junior mining over the past year. Early retail investors buy on high hopes before results. Smart institutional investors are willing to pay higher for real results from those disappointed by real results.
Eric Sprott has been the go-to guy in mining over the past few years with being the main supporter behind Kirkland Lake (NYSE: KL ) and Novo Resources ( OTCQX:NSRPF ). Both companies have been the top performers over the past couple of years coming out of one of the worst bear markets where Eric Sprott was forced to distance himself from his company. Back in early 2015 he was relieved of his duties as portfolio manager.
What a turnaround it has been for Mr. Sprott since that time. Similar to when Steve Jobs was fired from Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), Sprott went on to turn around Kirkland Lake and Novo Resources.
Western Australia has taken the junior mining market by storm over the past year and a half led by Dr. Hennigh who runs Novo Resources which claims the Pilbara region could be home to the next Witwatersrand Gold Basin.
This company led by Dr. Hennigh and backed by famous junior mining financier Eric Sprott has seen its stock rise from pennies to as high as $8.50. Some of the newsletter writer pundits have targets of triple digits for the shares, claiming it to be the next and newest wits.
Similarly, Kirkland Lake, whose chairman is Eric Sprott, has been one of the top-performing producers increasing production year over year and at larger profits as costs have been low from recent financials.
As a junior mining investor for close to 25 years, I was very skeptical on Novo until I saw the recent news of the investment by Kirkland Lake. For those not so familiar with mining, Kirkland Lake has been one of the best turnaround stories in the sector and has attracted the who's who of shareholders including VanEck ( GDXJ ), Oppenheimer and Fidelity.
Here you have two 10 baggers, the real winners in the mining sector from both production and exploration standpoint, finally joining forces providing credibility. It appears everything points higher as Novo publishes the first two bulk samples from Comet Well and returns over 10 grams per tonne gold. See the news here .
Of course, the market does the opposite what most people expect. The market responded negatively gapping lower, down almost 30% on higher volume. Why?
Early retail investors with high hopes may be selling to institutions that are willing to pay higher for real results. There is still a lot of skepticism as this is a new and challenging system.
Investors must remember that Novo is still years away from production let alone a construction decision. Novo may be overvalued as each time it has produced results, it has been below expectations. The quick run to a 1+ billion market cap may have made it overvalued to other peers in the Pilbara with first-class assets and geological teams.
Despite today's gap down and selloff on the bulk sample news, it should not take away the credibility of the recent investment by Kirkland Lake. This is not just a decision by Sprott alone.
Kirkland Lake has some big funds behind it like Oppenheimer, Fidelity and VanEck. Obviously, the big time funds support this move now. It may be just the beginning and early retail investors may be looking for an excuse to sell. It appears the smart money is waiting to buy as they prove this area technically and are willing to pay higher as the project is derisked.
However, one can't deny the potential with the Kirkland Lake backing to build a major over the long term. Kirkland paid $5 for Novo's stock, and the stock is trading significantly below that now. It didn't pay $20 million for stock for something that doesn't have great potential.
This selloff may be a shakeout before some additional bulk sampling news. I wouldn't bet against Eric Sprott, Kirkland Lake and Novo; they have driven interest back into the mining sector when so many companies have been duds and underperformers.
Is this recent bulk sample news pullback a discount buying opportunity or is it signaling the end? Don't count Kirkland Lake and Eric Sprott out just on a one-day selloff. There could be more results coming that could reignite the gold rush taking place in the Pilbara in Western Australia.
I don't own shares of Novo, but am looking for other juniors building positions with much lower valuations in the Pilbara Region which if Kirkland Lake and Novo do well should come along for the ride.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
